questions.stem: RAJA RAMMOHAN ROY, the 'Father of Modern India' + 'Father of Bengal Renaissance', founded:
questions.explanation: RAJA RAMMOHAN ROY (1772-1833) — 'FATHER OF MODERN INDIA' + 'FATHER OF INDIAN RENAISSANCE' + 'MAKER OF MODERN INDIA'. Polymath — Sanskrit, Persian, Arabic, English, Bengali, Hebrew + Greek. Born Radhanagar, Hooghly (Bengal). Worked for British EIC for a period. FOUNDED: (1) ATMIYA SABHA (1815) — Kolkata discussion group. (2) BRAHMO SABHA (20 Aug 1828) — monotheistic + reformist; later formalised as BRAHMO SAMAJ (1830). Worshipped one impersonal God; rejected idolatry + caste + Vedic infallibility; emphasized reason + humanism. KEY CAMPAIGNS + REFORMS: (1) AGAINST SATI (widow immolation) — campaigned from 1811 (witnessed his sister-in-law's Sati). Got LORD WILLIAM BENTINCK to PASS REGULATION XVII of 1829 (SATI BAN) — effective 4 DEC 1829 in Bengal; extended to all of India by 1830. Orthodox Hindus opposed; Rammohan defended the law + travelled to UK to lobby against repeal. (2) Against CASTE discrimination + untouchability. (3) Against CHILD MARRIAGE + POLYGAMY; for WIDOW REMARRIAGE. (4) For WOMEN's EDUCATION + property rights. (5) For ENGLISH + WESTERN scientific education (influenced Macaulay's Minute 1835 + Wood's Despatch 1854). Supported HINDU COLLEGE Calcutta 1817 (with David Hare + Radhakanta Deb). (6) Against Christian proselytising without reason (wrote 'Precepts of Jesus' 1820 — Jesus as a moral teacher). PUBLICATIONS: (a) 'Tuhfat al-Muwahhidin' (Arabic, 1803-04, 'A Gift to Monotheists') — first major work, against idolatry + superstition. (b) 'SAMBAD KAUMUDI' (Bengali newspaper 1821) + 'MIRAT-UL-AKHBAR' (Persian 1822) — early pioneering journalism; fought Adam's Press Regulations (1823, restrictive). TITLE 'RAJA': given by MUGHAL emperor AKBAR II in 1830; sent to UK on behalf of him to plead for increased pension. Died in BRISTOL, ENGLAND, 27 Sep 1833; buried at Arnos Vale Cemetery (visited by Modi in 2015 + current Indian PMs). First High-Profile Indian to visit UK with public reception. Rammohan = architect of BENGAL RENAISSANCE (19TH C. movement — Vidyasagar, Debendranath + Keshab Chandra Sen, Swami Vivekananda, Bankim Chandra, Tagore all part of it). BRAHMO SAMAJ LATER SPLIT: (1) KESHUB CHANDRA SEN broke off → Brahmo Samaj of India (1866). (2) DEBENDRANATH TAGORE (Rabindranath's father) led ADI BRAHMO SAMAJ — more traditional. (3) Sadharan Brahmo Samaj (1878) — SHIBNATH SHASTRI. Together contributed to 19th-c. reformism. monotheistic reformist society; campaigned against SATI (1829 ban), caste, child marriage, polygamy; 1828, later BRAHMO SAMAJ.

questions.stem: ISHWAR CHANDRA VIDYASAGAR, Bengal reformer, is most famous for:
questions.explanation: ISHWAR CHANDRA VIDYASAGAR (26 Sep 1820 – 29 Jul 1891) — leading 19th-c. Bengali polymath — scholar, educator, reformer, writer. Born Birsingha village, Midnapore, Bengal (then Bengal Presidency) into a poor Brahmin family. Studied at Sanskrit College Calcutta 1829-41; graduated with distinction in Sanskrit literature + grammar + Vedanta + Samkhya + Nyaya + smriti. Got title 'VIDYASAGAR' ('Ocean of Knowledge') from Sanskrit College for his scholarship. Also learned English independently. SANSKRIT COLLEGE Principal 1851-58. MAJOR REFORMS: (1) HINDU WIDOW REMARRIAGE ACT XV of 1856 — his GREATEST campaign. Conducted systematic research citing Parashara Smriti texts (Manu smriti silent) that supported widow remarriage. Petitioned British Govt with 987 signatures including Rabindranath's grandfather Dwarkanath Tagore. LORD DALHOUSIE + LORD CANNING took it up; Act passed 26 July 1856. LEGAL + GREAT SOCIAL IMPACT on Hindu widows (previously forced into lifelong austerity, tonsure, white saree, fasts, forbidden from festivals). Vidyasagar married his son off to a widow to lead by example. Raised funds for widow remarriages. (2) WOMEN's EDUCATION — helped found 35 GIRLS' SCHOOLS in Bengal (incl. Bethune School 1849 with Drinkwater Bethune; the first secular girls' school in India). Supported Kadambini Ganguly (first female graduate + doctor, 1883). (3) Against POLYGAMY + CHILD MARRIAGE. (4) Opposed POLYGAMY among KULIN Brahmins. LITERARY: (1) 'BARNA PARICHAY' (1855) — BENGALI primer that REVOLUTIONISED Bengali script; used in every Bengali school for 150+ years. (2) 'BETAL PANCHABINGSATI' (translations of Vetala Panchavimshati). (3) 'SHAKUNTALA' (Kalidasa translation). (4) 'SEETAR BANABAS' (1860). (5) 'BRIDDHABIBAHO' (polygamy essay). Vidyasagar's PROSE style shaped modern Bengali. PEDAGOGY: Sanskrit College Principal; opened Sanskrit study to non-Brahmins — radical; modernised curriculum incorporating Western philosophy, logic; English medium for higher learning. BARNAPARICHAY + his 1858 resignation from Sanskrit College (over administration issues) — set him as independent public figure. Also founded several OTHER schools (e.g., METROPOLITAN INSTITUTION, Kolkata, 1864 — now VIDYASAGAR COLLEGE). DEATH: 29 Jul 1891. RABINDRANATH TAGORE wrote VIDYASAGAR Charit — an essay. Ashoka Gupta + others wrote biographies. 200th birth anniversary celebrated 2020. UNION MP RC DEB + PM Modi's frequent tributes. OTHER Bengal reformers: (a) KESHAB CHANDRA SEN — Brahmo leader, Navavidhan; Swami Vivekananda's Ramakrishna association. (b) DEBENDRANATH TAGORE — Adi Brahmo. (c) DAYANANDA SARASWATI — Arya Samaj (Mumbai 1875). (d) SWAMI VIVEKANANDA — Chicago Parliament of Religions 1893; Ramakrishna Mission 1897. secured legalisation of Hindu widow remarriage (ACT XV of 1856); also championed women's education + modernised Bengali primer.

questions.stem: SWAMI DAYANANDA SARASWATI founded which reform movement with the motto 'BACK TO THE VEDAS'?
questions.explanation: SWAMI DAYANANDA SARASWATI (1824-1883) — Gujarati-born Hindu reformer; founder of ARYA SAMAJ. Born Mool Shankar Tiwari in Tankara, Gujarat, into a Shaiva Brahmin family. As a young boy, during Shivaratri vigil (age 14), he saw mice eating offerings on Shiva lingam — questioned idol worship. Left home at 22; became sannyasi; studied Vedas with SWAMI VIRAJANANDA at Mathura; emerged as reformer. Name 'Dayananda Saraswati' given by Virajananda. FOUNDED ARYA SAMAJ — 10 APRIL 1875 at BOMBAY (later HQ moved to Lahore). PRINCIPLES + 10 tenets: (1) God is sole creator + sustainer + destroyer — formless, eternal, unchangeable; (2) Vedas are INFALLIBLE + sole religious authority ('Back to the Vedas'); (3) Rituals only if rational + for good; (4) No idolatry (murti puja rejected); (5) No caste by birth (emphasis on 'Vedic varna' by qualities); (6) No untouchability; (7) No polygamy, child marriage, Sati, dowry; (8) Women's rights including education + property inheritance + widow remarriage; (9) SHUDDHI (reconversion / purification) of Hindus who had converted to Islam or Christianity — pioneered by Arya Samaj; (10) universal brotherhood. BOOKS: (1) SATYARTH PRAKASH ('Light of Truth', 1875) — MAGNUM OPUS; in Hindi; 14 chapters; comprehensive critique of all religions + Hindu practices; blueprint for reform. (2) RIGVEDADI-BHASHYA-BHUMIKA. (3) BIBLIOGRAPHICAL NOTES on VEDAS. INFLUENCE: INDIA's FIRST SOCIAL REFORM MOVEMENT to spread among WORKING-CLASS + rural areas (vs. Brahmo Samaj's elite Bengali base). Arya Samaj ran SCHOOLS + DAV colleges (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic, first at Lahore 1886 — now 900+ DAV institutions worldwide). EDUCATION + GIRLS' EDUCATION (KANYA MAHAVIDYALAYA, Jalandhar 1896). GURUKUL PATH at Kangri (Haridwar 1902) by Swami Shraddhanand. VEDIC research + publications. MAJOR Arya Samaj influenced leaders: LALA LAJPAT RAI, LALA HANS RAJ, SWAMI SHRADDHANAND (killed 1926 by Muslim fanatic for shuddhi activities), BHAGAT SINGH's uncle Ajit Singh, BHAI PARMANAND, Lala Hardayal (Ghadar Party), Madam Cama, various Punjab + UP political leaders. MOTHER INDIA: the phrase + the term 'Aryavarta' revived. DAYANANDA DIED 1883, AJMER — allegedly POISONED on orders of Jodhpur king's court (disputes). ARYA SAMAJ strongest in Punjab, Haryana, UP, Delhi; ~10 million+ adherents worldwide (diaspora — Surinam, Mauritius, Trinidad, Fiji, South Africa, Kenya, UK, USA). COMPARISON with Brahmo Samaj: both reform, but Brahmo softer (Unitarian flavour) + Arya more assertive + culturally nationalist. DAYANANDA's legacy critical of British rule inspired later nationalism. Bhagat Singh's atheism emerged by questioning Arya Samaj certainty. rejected idolatry + caste; emphasized Vedas as sole authority; Satyarth Prakash (1875); radical social reform + education; 1875, Bombay.

questions.stem: SWAMI VIVEKANANDA's famous address at the WORLD'S PARLIAMENT OF RELIGIONS (Chicago, 1893) began with:
questions.explanation: SWAMI VIVEKANANDA (12 Jan 1863 – 4 Jul 1902) — iconic Indian monk; chief disciple of RAMAKRISHNA PARAMAHAMSA; founder of RAMAKRISHNA MISSION (1897); introduced VEDANTA + YOGA to the WESTERN world. Birth name: NARENDRA NATH DATTA. Born Calcutta, educated at Presidency College + Scottish Church College. Met RAMAKRISHNA (Dakshineswar Kali temple priest) in 1881; became his most devoted disciple. After Ramakrishna's death (1886), led monastic brotherhood at Baranagar + took sannyas name 'Vivekananda'. CHICAGO 1893 — PARLIAMENT OF RELIGIONS (first of its kind globally; 11-27 Sep 1893; part of World's Columbian Exposition). Vivekananda arrived with no invitation + no organisational backing; introduced by Prof. J.H. Wright of Harvard (who famously wrote: 'To ask for your credentials is like asking the sun to state its right to shine'). 11 SEPTEMBER 1893 — HIS DEBUT ADDRESS began with 'SISTERS AND BROTHERS OF AMERICA' — got a 2-MINUTE STANDING OVATION from 7,000 audience members (none had greeted them thus — typical 'Ladies + Gentlemen'). Spoke about religious tolerance + Hinduism's universal acceptance. 11 Sep 1893 known as 'VIVEKANANDA's DAY'; India's NATIONAL YOUTH DAY (12 Jan, his birthday). SUBSEQUENT: toured USA + UK for 4 YEARS; founded VEDANTA SOCIETY in NYC (1894); returned to India 1897 to hero's welcome; founded RAMAKRISHNA MISSION on 1 MAY 1897 at Belur Math, Howrah (HQ, near Kolkata; now a world-headquartered order with 225+ branches). Ramakrishna Math (monastic) + Ramakrishna Mission (service) + Belur Math. TEACHINGS: (1) 'SHIVA JNANE JIVA SEVA' — 'service to man is service to God'; every human has divine spark; serve humanity = serve God. (2) 'Arise, awake + stop not till the goal is reached' (from Katha Upanishad). (3) Muscular spirituality; emphasised strength, self-confidence, positive thinking. (4) Promoted Vedanta (non-dualistic Advaita) globally. (5) Defended Hinduism vs Christian missionary + colonial critique. (6) Supported women's education + empowerment (influenced Sister Nivedita / Margaret Noble — Irish disciple). (7) Rejected caste. WORKS: (1) KARMA YOGA + BHAKTI YOGA + JNANA YOGA + RAJA YOGA — 4 paths of yoga lectures in USA (1896). (2) 'Colombo to Almora Lectures'. (3) Speeches compiled in multiple volumes. (4) SONGS to Kali. DIED 4 July 1902, Belur Math (age 39, Mahasamadhi). LEGACY: (a) India's first global 'cultural ambassador'; (b) inspired RAMAKRISHNA VIVEKANANDA VEDANTA MOVEMENT worldwide; (c) Swami Tejomayananda + current Swami Gautamananda; (d) Tagore, Gandhi, Subhas Bose, Rolland, Aurobindo + later India's leaders drew inspiration. Vivekananda Rock Memorial at Kanyakumari (1970). Ramakrishna Mission runs ~140+ hospitals, schools, relief work globally. received 2-minute standing ovation; became global face of Hindu spirituality + yoga.

questions.stem: JYOTIRAO (JYOTIBA) PHULE + his wife SAVITRIBAI PHULE were PIONEERS of:
questions.explanation: JYOTIRAO GOVINDRAO PHULE (11 Apr 1827 – 28 Nov 1890) + his wife SAVITRIBAI PHULE (3 Jan 1831 – 10 Mar 1897) — 19th-c. social reformers in Maharashtra; revolutionary against CASTE OPPRESSION + for WOMEN's + LOWER-CASTE EDUCATION. Jyotiba's Mali caste (gardener/cultivator) was classified 'Shudra' — oppressed. REFORMS: (1) JANUARY 1848 — opened INDIA's FIRST GIRLS' SCHOOL at Bhide Wada, Pune — Savitribai taught the 8 students. She thus became INDIA'S FIRST WOMAN TEACHER. Opposed by orthodox Hindus (Savitribai faced abuse — cow dung + stones thrown at her en route; wore extra sari to change before teaching). Phules later opened ~17-18 schools for girls, untouchables, widows. (2) 1851 — Phules opened a GIRLS' SCHOOL specifically for UNTOUCHABLE (Dalit) children. (3) 1863 — established an HOME FOR CHILD-BEARING WIDOWS + ORPHANS (Balhatya Pratibandhak Griha) — rescued pregnant Brahmin widows from infanticide; adopted a Brahmin widow's son Yashwant Rao. (4) Campaigned against CHILD MARRIAGE, SATI, caste restrictions, enforced WIDOWHOOD. (5) Opened first DRINKING WATER well in Pune for 'untouchable' use (common well was denied to them). (6) Named their movement 'TRUTH SEEKERS' SOCIETY' — SATYASHODHAK SAMAJ founded 24 SEPTEMBER 1873 by Jyotiba — rejected caste, Brahmin priesthood, demanded rationality + social justice. Non-Brahmin priests for rituals. BOOKS by JYOTIBA: (1) 'GULAMGIRI' ('Slavery', 1873) — landmark; dedicated to American abolitionists — parallel between American slavery + Indian caste oppression. Direct critique of Brahmin supremacy. (2) 'SHETKARYACHA ASUD' ('Cultivator's Whipcord', 1881) — on farmer exploitation. (3) 'Sarvajanik Satya Dharma Pustak' (1891, posthumous). POETRY by SAVITRIBAI — 'Kavya Phule' (1854) + 'Bavan Kashi Subodh Ratnakar' (1892); first female Marathi poet of modern era. DIED: Jyotiba 1890; Savitribai 10 March 1897 NURSING PLAGUE PATIENTS during Pune bubonic plague (1896-97 Pune) — caught plague, died. 'Mahatma' title given to Jyotiba on 11 May 1888 by Mumbai public function. LEGACY: (1) PHULES' work inspired BR AMBEDKAR (who cited Phule as one of his gurus — with Buddha + Kabir); (2) laid foundation of ANTI-CASTE + DALIT rights movement; (3) BAHUJAN (majority low-caste) movement; (4) MAHARASHTRA's strong reform tradition. Savitribai's birth anniversary 3 JAN = MAHARASHTRA GIRL EDUCATION DAY since 2015. Pune University renamed SAVITRIBAI PHULE PUNE UNIVERSITY (2014). Phule-Shahu-Ambedkar trinity of Maharashtra reform. SHAHUJI MAHARAJ of Kolhapur — princely reformer + ally of the Phules + influence on Ambedkar; introduced RESERVATION for non-Brahmins in Kolhapur state 1902 (50% — FIRST reservation policy in India).

questions.stem: Dr B.R. AMBEDKAR is known as the 'ARCHITECT OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION' + champion of Dalit rights. He converted along with ~5 lakh followers to:
questions.explanation: Dr. BHIMRAO RAMJI AMBEDKAR (14 Apr 1891 – 6 Dec 1956) — Indian jurist, economist, politician, social reformer; first LAW Minister of India; architect + Chairman of DRAFTING COMMITTEE of the CONSTITUTION of INDIA; principal champion of DALIT RIGHTS. Born Mhow, MP, into MAHAR family (Dalit caste, then 'untouchable') — extensive experience of caste discrimination from childhood. EDUCATION: Elphinstone College Mumbai BA 1912; Columbia University (USA) MA 1915 + PhD 1927 (economics; 'The Evolution of Provincial Finance in British India'); LSE MSc 1921 + DSc 1923; Gray's Inn Bar-at-Law 1923. First ASIAN with a PhD in Economics. ACTIVISM: (1) 1924 — BAHISHKRIT HITAKARINI SABHA founded in Bombay for Dalit welfare. (2) 1927 — MAHAD SATYAGRAHA (Chowdar Tank) — Dalits claimed right to drink public water; burned Manusmriti copy (25 Dec 1927). (3) 1930s — founded political parties; Dalit rights advocacy. (4) 1930-32 — ROUND TABLE CONFERENCES in London (sole Dalit spokesperson); demanded separate electorates for Depressed Classes — granted by Communal Award 1932 but Gandhi opposed; POONA PACT 24 Sep 1932 — joint electorates with reserved seats. (5) 1936 — 'Annihilation of Caste' (his greatest treatise, undelivered speech). (6) 1942-46 — Labour Member, Viceroy's Executive Council. (7) CONSTITUTION: (1946-49) — Constituent Assembly member from Bombay; CHAIRMAN OF DRAFTING COMMITTEE from 29 Aug 1947. Drafted CONSTITUTION in collaboration with advisor B.N. RAO + members (Munshi, Ayyar, Madhava Rao, Saadullah, Khaitan, Mitter, Gopalaswami Ayyangar). 'FATHER OF CONSTITUTION' title. Championed (a) secular republic; (b) FRs + DPSPs; (c) RESERVATIONS for SC/ST in legislatures + education + govt jobs; (d) abolition of untouchability (Art 17); (e) equality + rule of law. (8) POST-independence: LAW MINISTER in Nehru's cabinet 1947-51. PIONEERED HINDU CODE BILL (sought to codify + reform Hindu personal law — women's rights to property, divorce, polygamy ban). OPPOSED by conservatives; partially implemented only post-1955; Ambedkar RESIGNED Sept 1951 over stalled progress. (9) 14 OCTOBER 1956, DEEKSHABHOOMI, NAGPUR — CONVERTED TO BUDDHISM along with ~3.8 LAKH followers (largest religious conversion ceremony in modern history). Took 22 vows rejecting Hinduism. Founded NAVAYANA BUDDHISM (modern egalitarian Buddhism). DIED 6 Dec 1956 at Delhi (just 2 months later), age 65. 6 DEC = MAHAPARINIRVAN DIWAS. BHARAT RATNA posthumous 1990 (belated). LEGACY: 'DALIT MESSIAH', 'Bodhisattva', father of Indian Constitution. 14 APRIL = AMBEDKAR JAYANTI (national holiday since 2016). Statue at Parliament + Ambedkar Memorial Delhi. Books: 'Who were the Shudras?', 'The Untouchables: Who Were They?', 'Buddha and his Dhamma', 'Thoughts on Pakistan'. 4 books on Indian currency. Bhim Jayanti, Dr B.R. AMBEDKAR Open University. 14 Oct 1956 at Nagpur (Deekshabhoomi); mass conversion ceremony; revived Navayana Buddhism; died 6 Dec 1956 (just 2 months later).

questions.stem: PERIYAR (E.V. Ramasamy), leader of the DRAVIDIAN Self-Respect Movement in Tamil Nadu, is most associated with:
questions.explanation: E.V. RAMASAMY 'PERIYAR' (17 Sep 1879 – 24 Dec 1973) — Tamil social reformer + politician; leader of the SELF-RESPECT MOVEMENT + the DRAVIDIAN MOVEMENT. 'PERIYAR' = 'RESPECTED ONE' / 'GRAND OLD MAN'; title conferred 1938 by 9th Tamil Nadu Women's Conference. Born Erode, TN to a Kannada-speaking Balija Naidu family (ironic given his later Dravidian militancy). EARLY LIFE: merchant; joined Indian National Congress 1919 at Gandhi's Champaran call; active in Vaikom Satyagraha 1924 (fought for Dalit right to walk temple roads in Travancore; called 'Vaikom Veeran' — hero of Vaikom; jailed). Disillusioned with Congress 1925 over caste discrimination issues — left party 1925. FOUNDED: (1) SELF-RESPECT MOVEMENT (1925, Kudi Arasu newspaper) — rationalist + anti-caste + anti-religion + anti-hindutva. Promoted 'Self-Respect Marriages' (no priest + no religious rituals + no astrology). (2) JUSTICE PARTY membership 1935 (earlier founded 1916 by Pitti Tyagaraya Chetty + Natesa Mudaliar + T.M. Nair — first non-Brahmin party challenging Brahmin domination in Madras Presidency). (3) 1938 — Anti-Hindi Agitation in Madras Presidency when CM Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) made Hindi compulsory — violent protests; 2 deaths (Thalamuthu + Natarajan); Hindi order withdrawn 1940. Solidified Tamil linguistic nationalism. (4) 1944 — Renamed Justice Party as 'DRAVIDAR KAZHAGAM' (DK); demanded SEPARATE DRAVIDA NADU (for Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam peoples) — later dropped the separation demand. (5) 1949 — His protégé C.N. ANNADURAI broke off DK → founded DRAVIDA MUNNETRA KAZHAGAM (DMK); Periyar stayed with DK. (6) 1967 — DMK swept TN assembly elections; Annadurai = CM; end of Congress era in TN; Tamil politics became Dravidian-dominated ever since (DMK + later AIADMK split 1972 by MGR). IDEOLOGY: (1) RATIONALISM — atheist; rejected all religions; burned Manusmriti + Ramayana copies ('RAVANA is the HERO' — reversed reading of Ramayana); saw Brahmanism as tool of North Indian / Aryan domination of South Indian / Dravidian people. (2) ANTI-BRAHMIN + anti-caste; advocated self-respect + human dignity. (3) WOMEN'S RIGHTS — contraception, widow remarriage, property rights, against child marriage; radical for 1920s. (4) Anti-Hindi; pro-Tamil identity. (5) Rejected 'India' as a construct + 'Hindi-Hindu-Hindustan' slogan. (6) Called 'SOCRATES OF SOUTH ASIA' by UNESCO 1970. DIED 24 Dec 1973; statue at Vaikom Kerala. IMPACT: Tamil Nadu remains DRAVIDIAN political stronghold (DMK — MK Stalin CM 2021-present; AIADMK); non-Brahmin reservation policy + social justice benchmark in TN. PERIYAR NAIDU CENTER + Memorial at Erode. fought Brahmin supremacy + Hindi imposition; advocated separate Dravida Nadu briefly; championed women's + Dalit rights.

questions.stem: Which reformer is called the 'GRAND OLD MAN OF INDIA' + wrote 'POVERTY + UN-BRITISH RULE IN INDIA' proving the DRAIN of wealth from India?
questions.explanation: DADABHAI NAOROJI (4 Sep 1825 – 30 Jun 1917) — 'GRAND OLD MAN OF INDIA'; 'PITAMAHA OF INDIAN NATIONALISM'; 'UNOFFICIAL AMBASSADOR OF INDIA'. Born in Bombay Parsi family. Studied Elphinstone Institution — first Indian to be Professor (Maths + Natural Philosophy, 1855). ACHIEVEMENTS: (1) FIRST ASIAN to become a BRITISH MP — elected 1892 from FINSBURY CENTRAL (London) as Liberal Party candidate, serving 1892-95. Won by just 5 votes. Salisbury had earlier remarked 'a black man cannot be elected to the British Parliament' — Naoroji proved him wrong. Later Mancherjee Bhownagree (1895-1906, Conservative) + Shapurji Saklatvala (1922-1929, Communist) became 2nd + 3rd Indian MPs. (2) THRICE PRESIDENT of INDIAN NATIONAL CONGRESS — (a) 1886 Calcutta (2nd session); (b) 1893 Lahore; (c) 1906 Calcutta (Swaraj session). (3) 1906 CONGRESS — FIRST to explicitly demand 'SELF-GOVERNMENT' / 'SWARAJ' as a goal. (4) Founded the EAST INDIA ASSOCIATION (1866, London) — to present Indian grievances to British public + Parliament; precursor of Congress. DRAIN THEORY: Naoroji's MAJOR intellectual + political contribution. Thesis: BRITISH drained Indian wealth out of the country via salaries + pensions of British officials in India, home charges, ship transport, exports under-priced, imports over-priced, interest on public debt. Developed through years of ECONOMIC study + lectures 1860s-1900s. (a) 'ENGLAND'S DEBT TO INDIA' (1867 lecture, London). (b) 'POVERTY OF INDIA' (1876, pamphlet). (c) 'POVERTY + UN-BRITISH RULE IN INDIA' (1901 — seminal book; estimated DRAIN at ~£30 million per year, equivalent to 20-30% of India's annual revenue; per-capita income of India ₹20/year in 1867-68 — LESS THAN cost of a decent meal). Showed India's economic backwardness was MADE, not inherent. His drain theory armed later nationalists — GOKHALE (his protégé), TILAK, RANADE, R.C. DUTT (author of 'Economic History of India' 1902-04). INSPIRED GANDHI (who called him 'Dada', father-figure; Gandhi's South Africa work supported by him). Influenced Nehru's economic views (mixed economy, planning). MEMORIALS: Dadabhai Naoroji Road in most Indian cities; at Flora Fountain in Mumbai. Bharatiya Arts + Culture Award. Early 20TH c INC 'Moderates' — Naoroji, Gokhale, Surendranath Banerjee, Pherozeshah Mehta, Dinshaw Wacha, Dutt, Phirojshah (leader of Bombay triumvirate + Congress), W.C. Bonnerjee (first INC President 1885 Bombay). Approach: CONSTITUTIONAL agitation, petitions, prayers, appealing to British sense of justice. Replaced by EXTREMISTS (Tilak + Lajpat + Pal) post-1905 Bengal Partition. first Asian British MP (Liberal Party, Finsbury 1892-95); 3-time INC President; first to quantify COLONIAL DRAIN.

questions.stem: The THEOSOPHICAL SOCIETY in India was associated with:

options.option_text: ANNIE BESANT + Col. OLCOTT + Madame Blavatsky

questions.explanation: THEOSOPHICAL SOCIETY — spiritualist + reformist organisation. FOUNDED: 17 NOV 1875 in NEW YORK CITY by HELENA PETROVNA BLAVATSKY (Madame Blavatsky, Russian-born) + Col. HENRY STEEL OLCOTT (American) + William Quan Judge. HEADQUARTERS moved to ADYAR, CHENNAI (then Madras) in 1882. Adyar HQ since 1886 became international centre. OBJECTIVES ('3 OBJECTS'): (1) To form a nucleus of the UNIVERSAL BROTHERHOOD of Humanity; (2) To encourage the study of comparative RELIGION, PHILOSOPHY + SCIENCE; (3) To investigate unexplained laws of Nature + the powers LATENT in man. Emphasis on UNIVERSAL SPIRITUAL WISDOM ('Theosophy' = divine wisdom); syncretic; drew from Hindu + Buddhist + Egyptian + Christian mysticism, Kabbalah + Western occult. ANNIE BESANT (1 Oct 1847 – 20 Sep 1933) — British-born socialist, women's rights activist, freethinker, orator; joined Theosophical Society 1889; MOVED to INDIA 1893; succeeded Olcott as PRESIDENT of Theosophical Society 1907. Stayed in India till death. CONTRIBUTIONS: (1) CHAMPIONED Hindu revival + reform — edited 'The Commonweal' + 'New India' newspapers. (2) Founded CENTRAL HINDU COLLEGE, Banaras (1898) with MADAN MOHAN MALAVIYA — nucleus of BANARAS HINDU UNIVERSITY (BHU, 1916). (3) Opened girls' school in Varanasi. (4) HOME RULE MOVEMENT — founded INDIAN HOME RULE LEAGUE in 1916 (Tilak founded a parallel one in Maharashtra same year; both coordinated). Demanded SELF-GOVERNMENT within British Empire (Dominion Status like Canada/Australia). Led massive civil agitation. Arrested 1917 by Madras govt; agitation intensified; released. Chosen as CONGRESS PRESIDENT in CALCUTTA SESSION 1917 — FIRST WOMAN President of INC. (5) Discovered + popularised J. KRISHNAMURTI (1895-1986) at Adyar — believing him a future 'World Teacher' / Maitreya; groomed him as the head of 'Order of the Star in the East'; Krishnamurti later DISSOLVED the Order (1929) + rejected all authority-based spirituality; became an iconic independent philosopher. (6) WORKS: 'Why I Became A Theosophist' (1889), 'Ancient Wisdom', 'Esoteric Christianity', 'India: A Nation' (1915). Translated BHAGAVAD GITA. OTHER NOTABLES of Theosophical Society: (a) CHARLES LEADBEATER — clairvoyant author. (b) GEORGE ARUNDALE — later president. (c) NEHRU as young man attended Theosophy lectures. (d) Gandhi first READ GITA (in English translation) at Theosophical Society meetings in London (1890s). INFLUENCE: brought Hindu-Buddhist ideas to Western audiences; countered missionary discrediting of Hinduism; fed Indian cultural + national confidence; bridge between East + West. DECLINE after 1920s as freedom struggle focused elsewhere; ATTENDANCE still at Adyar (one of the most beautiful HQ campuses). Adyar Library — valuable collection of Sanskrit manuscripts. founded 1875 New York; HQ Adyar Chennai from 1882; championed Hindu revival + Indian home rule (1916).

questions.stem: Which Muslim reformer founded MUHAMMADAN ANGLO-ORIENTAL COLLEGE at ALIGARH in 1875, which became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920?
questions.explanation: SIR SYED AHMAD KHAN (17 Oct 1817 – 27 Mar 1898) — 19th-c. Indian Muslim reformer + educationist + founder of the ALIGARH MOVEMENT. Born Delhi to noble Mughal-era family; educated at home in Arabic + Persian + Islamic studies + mathematics. Joined EIC judicial service 1838; loyal servant of the British throughout. KEY CONTRIBUTIONS: (1) SAVED many British lives during 1857 REVOLT at Bijnor (where he was Sadr Amin); stayed loyal. (2) Wrote 'ASBAB-E-BAGHAWAT-E-HIND' ('Causes of the Indian Revolt', 1859) — analytical account; criticised British mistakes that caused revolt (denied government of Indians by Indians, missionary arrogance, cow-cartridges, etc.) but also criticised Muslim backwardness + urged modernisation. Published 1873 in English. (3) Visited LONDON 1869-70; impressed by Cambridge + Oxford; decided to build similar institution for Muslims. (4) FOUNDED 'MUHAMMADAN ANGLO-ORIENTAL COLLEGE' (MAO COLLEGE) at ALIGARH, UP on 24 MAY 1875 — patterned on Cambridge; offered MODERN ENGLISH + SCIENTIFIC education along with Islamic studies. Elevated to ALIGARH MUSLIM UNIVERSITY in 1920 (by Indian Legislative Council Act). (5) Founded SCIENTIFIC SOCIETY (1864, Aligarh) to translate Western scientific + literary works into Urdu. (6) Edited 'TAHZIB-UL-AKHLAQ' ('Social Reformer', 1870s magazine) — reformist writings. (7) Introduced MODERN INTERPRETATION of Quran compatible with science + rationality; emphasised ALLEGORICAL reading of supernatural elements (jinn, miracles). Wrote 'TAFSIR-UL-QURAN'. (8) Opposed PURDAH + polygamy; advocated women's education later in life. (9) Opposed INC (Indian National Congress 1885) — feared it dominated by Hindu majority; instead called for Muslim political separation from INC. TWO-NATION precursor views. Started ALL-INDIA MUHAMMADAN EDUCATIONAL CONFERENCE 1886 — politically informed Muslim League (1906 Dacca). HONOURS: knighted 1888 (KCSI); DCL by Edinburgh 1889. LEGACY: (a) BELOVED founder-figure of AMU; Strachey HALL + SYED HALL buildings. (b) 'FATHER OF MUSLIM MODERNISM in INDIA'; (c) Aligarh Movement produced generations of Muslim leaders — Mohsin-ul-Mulk, Viqar-ul-Mulk, Maulana Muhammad Ali (Khilafat), Shibli Nomani, Hasrat Mohani, Zakir Hussain (later President of India), many Pakistani leaders (Liaqat Ali Khan, Ayub Khan connections via AMU), + many Indian leaders. (d) Aligarh vs Darul Uloom DEOBAND (1867, Shah Waliullah's traditionalist school — Mohammad Qasim Nanotvi + Rashid Ahmad Gangohi) — Aligarh modernist + pro-British; Deoband Traditional + anti-British + pro-INC (Jamiat Ulama-e-Hind 1919 closely with Congress). Ratna Bharat Ratna did not receive. (e) Negative legacy: some historians trace seeds of Muslim separatism + Partition to Aligarh's communal politics. OTHER Muslim social reformers: (a) BADRUDDIN TYABJI — Bombay, 3rd INC President (1887). (b) MAULANA ABUL KALAM AZAD — scholar, Congress President (2 terms), education minister independent India. Aligarh Movement; advocated modern English + scientific education for Muslims; loyalty to British; opposed 1857 revolt.
